instructions: At least 1 hour ahead: in a large bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder, tapioca starch, custard powder, eggs, sugar, evaporated milk, 150 ml (2/3 cup) water, 1 tbsp of the oil and the vanilla. Whisk until only a few small lumps are left. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.

Check whether your egg waffle pan can go straight on the stove. If it can't, set it on a wire rack over the burner. Heat both halves over medium-high for 1 to 2 minutes. (With an electric bubble waffle maker, preheat it and follow its directions from step 4.)
Brush both halves with the remaining 1 tbsp oil. Don't use cooking spray. Turn the heat down to medium.

Pour 3/4 cup of the batter into the center of the pan, close it firmly, and flip it right away. Cook for about 2 minutes, flip, and cook 2 minutes. Keep flipping every couple of minutes until the waffle is golden brown. Timing depends on your stove, so treat the first waffle as a test.
Hold the pan over a plate with the waffle side down. Loosen the waffle from the top edge with a chopstick or spoon and let it curl and drop out.
Re-oil the pan and repeat with the rest of the batter. Serve right away.
advance_prep_notes: batter needs to rest in the fridge at least 1 hour
method_notes: Only a few versions are rated, and none has 20 ratings, so the lead is Kirbie's Cravings (5 from 10). It and Hungry Huy (5 from 1) agree on the batter: flour, tapioca starch, custard powder, eggs, sugar, evaporated milk, a 1 hour rest, and a hot greased egg waffle pan. Hungry Huy's batter is thinner and cooks 5 to 7 minutes in total. The dish needs an egg waffle pan or an electric bubble waffle maker.
